born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when starvation is imminent, uses history to avoid known poisons, and strategically tastes unknown fruits only when safe enough to learn without risking death, ensuring long-term foraging efficiency.

The code improves survival by preventing suicidal tasting of unknown fruits when hunger is critical, and by prioritizing carrying known-safe foods to build a pantry reserve for future starvation events.

This code improves survival by prioritizing the accumulation of a safe food stash when hunger is moderate, while maintaining cautious learning for unknown fruits and immediate consumption only when starving or when a stash already exists to avoid unnecessary carrying effort.
The code prioritizes survival by eating when critically starved, avoiding known poisons, tasting unknowns to gather data when safe, and eating known-safefruits when not already carrying a load.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when starvation is imminent (hunger > 98), uses tasting to safely identify new species without full consumption risk, and carries known safe fruits when hunger is moderate to save foraging time, while strictly avoiding any fruit with a history of causing harm.

The code improves safety by grouping fruits into "species" based on shared traits (key, smell, color); if any fruit with those traits was previously identified as poisonous, the ant avoids them unless it is the specific target or starving. This prevents repeated mistakes with similar-looking fruits while maintaining a functional emergency starvation protocol and curiosity-driven tasting for unknowns.

The code prioritizes survival by eating critical starvation risks, uses tasting for unknowns when safe, and optimizes energy intake by carrying known safe foods when hunger is moderate or the fruit is targeted, while avoiding poisonous species identified by past harm.
